newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran Feb CPI up 2.4 pct,threatening '97 target.
newsitem.headline: Honduran Feb CPI up 2.4 pct,threatening '97 target.

text.p: Consumer inflation in Honduras rose 2.4 percent in February, seriously threatening the government goal of 15 percent inflation for 1997, a Central Bank economist said on Friday.
Cumulative inflation through the first two months of the year reached 4.5 percent, economist Martin Barahona told Reuters.
"We should expect inflation well above 15 percent for 1997)," Barahona said. "Based on inflation for January and February, we can expect the same will happen the rest of the year."
This year's February inflation was up from 2.0 percent in February 1996, and the cumulative rate is up from 3.6 percent in the first two months of last year.
Fueling last month's rise in consumer prices were education costs, up 9.3 percent, an increase largely due to higher school fees.
Health care costs rose 4.0 percent and food prices were up 2.1 percent, the Central Bank said.
Year-over-year inflation through February 1997 was 26.8 percent, up from 21.4 percent in the previous 12-month period.
